summary: Treasury says PARECO-FF controlled Rubaya mining sites from 2022 until early 2024, when M23 took over.
notes: End date set to the eve of the M23 takeover; Treasury says only 'early 2024'.

summary: UN Group of Experts: AFC/M23 has occupied Rubaya town and the whole surrounding mining area since 30 April 2024.
UN Group of Experts: M23 taxed Rubaya coltan at $7/kg and cassiterite at $4/kg, collecting at least US$800,000 a month.
UN Group of Experts: M23 controlled transport routes from Rubaya to Rwanda and ensured a monopoly on Rubaya coltan exports to Rwanda.
UN Group of Experts: M23 controlled the Rubaya and Mushaki trading centres.
notes: No separate start date given; shown from the report date (Dec 2024).

summary: Amnesty: M23 forced the mining cooperatives out of Lomera in April–May 2025, then taxed miners and controlled the site, working with a company and Rwandan nationals.
notes: Corrected from Apr 2025: the UN dates M23 control to mid-February 2025 and Amnesty dates the expulsion of cooperatives to Apr–May 2025. The site has reportedly been closed since about September 2025.

summary: Global Witness: since M23 took Goma, coltan often crosses into Rwanda openly at the Grande Barrière crossing in view of Rwandan border officials.
UN experts: from early February 2025 AFC/M23 held exclusive control of the key mineral trading centre at Numbi.
UN experts: from early February 2025 AFC/M23 held exclusive control of the key mineral trading centre at Nyabibwe.
Critical Threats reports M23 recaptured Numbi on 7 October as clashes went on. This is the fourth offensive in northern Kalehe since late June, so treat the hold as unstable.
UN experts: AFC/M23 took Nzibira on 21 September 2025. About 40 t a month of cassiterite and wolframite used to trade through it.

Actualite.cd reports repeated AFC/M23-Wazalendo fighting at Nzibira from 20 August 2026. Crisis Group says the government-side push toward Nzibira and Luntukulu did not produce a sustained advance, so M23 stays the likely holder.
